items.title: Parliament to debate new provinces next month, says minister
items.description:
Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said on Thursday that parliament was expected to debate the issue of new provinces next month.
Addressing the corporate sector in late July, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi had called for the creation of new provinces or administrative units, saying that the current system had “collapsed”.

items.title: Trump administration proposes waiving grace period for H-1B holders after job loss
items.description:
The Trump administration has proposed eliminating a 60-day grace period that allows certain immigrants, including skilled workers on H-1B visas, to stay in the United States and find a new sponsor after losing their job, according to a government notice posted online on Thursday.

items.description:
ISLAMABAD: The Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC) on Thursday directed universities to ensure that the Medical and Dental College Admission Test (MDCAT), scheduled for September 20, is conducted in a smooth and transparent manner.

items.description:

items.title: Death toll from cargo ship fire in China rises to 25: state media
items.description:
The death toll from a fire that erupted on Thursday on a foreign-flagged cargo ship docked in a Chinese port has risen to 25, including five people who had been listed as missing, state media said.
The bulk carrier, moored in the eastern shipping hub of Qingdao, had 42 people on board when the fire broke out, according to state broadcaster CCTV.
17 of those were evacuated, including five who were injured.
However, by Thursday evening “all 25 missing persons had been found, none showing signs of life”, state broadcaster CCTV reported.
It said “the open flames were extinguished” by about 2:30 pm

items.title: Anti-migrant protesters mistakenly target Pakistan U-19 team hotel in UK
items.description:
LONDON: Anti-immigration demonstrators in southern England massed outside a hotel where Pakistan’s U-19 cricket squad were staying after mistaking them for asylum seekers, British media reported on Wednesday.
The incident on Tuesday evening in a northern suburb of Portsmouth occurred some 48 hours after protesters disrupted the disembarkation of scores of migrants near the port city and confronted police in widely condemned scenes.
